facts.claim: struck seven times and survived each
facts.note: documented by the park superintendent, who witnessed none of them

facts.claim: first strike went through his leg and took his big toenail
facts.note: 1942, fire lookout tower: burned a strip down his right leg and hit his toe, left a hole in his shoe; the toenail detail is not on this page

facts.claim: struck in his own front yard
it set his hair on fire, twice
facts.note: source says his hair caught fire five times (1969, 1972, 1973, 1976, 1977); 'twice' undercounts. Suggest 'again and again'

facts.claim: people began to avoid him in storms
his wife was struck once in the yard beside him
facts.note: hanging clothes in the back yard; he was helping and was unharmed

facts.claim: Guinness: nobody struck more; called the human lightning rod
the odds of one strike are tiny, of seven almost beyond counting
facts.note: no figure checked; the plan shows no number on screen

facts.claim: died in 1983 aged 71; not from lightning
facts.note: September 28, 1983; the script leaves out the cause and so does the picture
